newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volkswagen says no change in EU standoff.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen says no change in EU standoff.

text.p: Volkswagen AG, Europe's largest auto maker, said on Tuesday there was no change in a standoff with Brussels over subsidies for plants in Saxony, despite reports a compromise was imminent.
A European Union source in Brussels said the European Commission was crafting a compromise with Bonn that would "neutralise" the 100 million marks ($67 million) in excess subsidies to VW.
Volkswagen spokesman Klaus Kocks said, "The basic situation has not changed. But VW will avoid an escalation." He declined to comment further.
A spokeswoman for the economics ministry in Bonn said that discussions were continuing.

The EU approved 540 million marks of a planned 780 million marks in proposed subsidies to VW to build two plants in the state of Saxony. But it says 100 million marks more than the approved amount have been illegally handed over to the auto maker.
VW has threatened in the past to take its investment elsewhere if the subsidies do not go through.
